name: Paroxetine
route_note: Oral tablets, controlled-release tablets, suspension; low-dose capsule for vasomotor symptoms.
owner: generic (many); GSK and Apotex (Paxil, by region)

discovery.note: Synthesised in the 1970s at Ferrosan and licensed to Beecham (later SmithKline Beecham/GSK). Year of the UK priority patent filing by Ferrosan.

tagline: Potent SSRI with anticholinergic effects and a marked discontinuation syndrome
summary: Paroxetine is a potent SSRI used for depression and a range of anxiety disorders. It is notable among SSRIs for its anticholinergic effects, strong CYP2D6 inhibition, short half-life with pronounced withdrawal symptoms, and controversies over its paediatric trials.
mechanism: Paroxetine is the most potent inhibitor of the serotonin transporter among the SSRIs, blocking serotonin reuptake into presynaptic neurons. It also has measurable affinity for muscarinic acetylcholine receptors and inhibits noradrenaline reuptake at higher doses.

It is a mechanism-based inhibitor of CYP2D6, which inhibits its own metabolism (non-linear kinetics) and raises levels of many co-administered drugs such as tamoxifen's activation pathway, codeine conversion and tricyclics.
uses: Moderate-to-severe vasomotor symptoms of menopause (7.5 mg, Brisdelle)

history.title: Development
history.detail: Paroxetine is developed at Ferrosan in Denmark in the 1970s and licensed to Beecham.

history.title: UK launch
history.detail: Paroxetine is launched in the UK as Seroxat.

history.title: FDA approval
history.detail: The FDA approves Paxil for depression in December 1992.

history.title: Study 329
history.detail: A GSK-sponsored trial of paroxetine in adolescent depression is published, later criticised for its reporting.

history.title: UK paediatric warning
history.detail: UK regulators advise against use in under-18s for depression after review of suicidality data.

history.title: Pregnancy warning
history.detail: The FDA warns of a possible increased risk of congenital cardiac malformations with first-trimester exposure.

history.title: GSK settlement
history.detail: GSK pleads guilty and pays $3 billion in a US settlement that includes unlawful promotion of Paxil for paediatric use.

history.title: Brisdelle
history.detail: Low-dose paroxetine mesylate becomes the first non-hormonal treatment approved for menopausal hot flushes.

history.title: Study 329 reanalysis
history.detail: A BMJ restoration reanalysis concludes paroxetine was neither effective nor safe in adolescents in that trial.

safety.boxed_warning: Increased risk of suicidal thoughts and behaviours in children, adolescents and young adults (under 25) taking antidepressants; monitor for clinical worsening.

facts: Paroxetine is one of the strongest clinical inhibitors of CYP2D6.
Study 329 became a landmark case in debates about selective reporting of clinical trials.
